# `ext::weighted_graph` — declaration reference

Generated source inventory. Linked guides own runtime and semantic contracts; a listed declaration does not establish executable behavior.

[All modules](../README.md) · [Source](../../../extended/ext/weighted_graph.lani#L3)

Layer: `ext`. Role: module. Profile: **Source inventory**.

Implemented canonical directed multigraphs with i64 costs: duplicates, parallel edges and self-loops remain. Raw construction copies and sorts without mutating input. Dijkstra rejects negative edges anywhere; Bellman-Ford rejects source-reachable negative cycles. Both check every examined reachable sum before improvement, retain the first equal-cost predecessor and return independently owned Paths. Size-based capacities, conservative work admission, explicit errors and manual cleanup are part of the contract. All four library gates pass on native Linux x86_64: direct storage/arithmetic/ownership/admission contracts, 2,819 model graphs/5,638 outcomes and five resource profiles with nine reached allocation failures and same-process recovery. Natural Overflow/NegativeCycle cleanup and two initial Dijkstra allocations with no traversal growth execute. The route-cost consumer passes all four groups/148 native cases, including three selected allocation failures and two real-stream chunk/prefix cases. These finite receipts exclude GPU-device execution, other targets and formal verification.

### function: dijkstra

[Source line 407](../../../extended/ext/weighted_graph.lani#L407)

```lanius
pub fn dijkstra(graph: View, source: i32, limits: Limits) -> core::result::Result<Paths,Error>
```

Validates, checks source/workspace/work admission, then rejects the first global negative arc before allocation. Lazy stale-entry filtering uses a reserved m+1 queue; checked-add overflow precedes improvement.

### function: bellman_ford

[Source line 471](../../../extended/ext/weighted_graph.lani#L471)

```lanius
pub fn bellman_ford(graph: View, source: i32, limits: Limits) -> core::result::Result<Paths,Error>
```

Canonical in-place strict relaxation for at most n-1 passes, followed by a reachable improvement scan. The first examined overflow or detected negative cycle wins; no partial Paths is returned.
